claim: Three full-section 5 m cap tests cost an unquoted $0.420–1.558M; use corrected rig reach and direct limits from CHECK-055.
source_report_body: MAINLINE-055 filed, QUESTIONABLE/PROJECTION. The cheapest test that turns gamma into evidence is three 5 m spherical caps on the true R10 curvature at full cross-section: 5052-O faces 3.10 mm, matched to Be's classical stiffness, on the real CR III 3/8-1.0 core. They are built with the route's seams and a reinforced edge, seeded with 2, 6 and 16 mm pole dimples, and loaded by evacuation plus a water head (sea level reaches gamma 0.593; 5 m of water 0.883). Cost USD 0.42-1.56M; an R30-similar pair adds 0.15-0.61M and a Be confirmation cap 1-4.6M. 038's 1 m foil/foam shells (30-90k) calibrate the elastic FE but cannot measure P2's gamma, because CHECK-029's core shear, face yield and core law are absent. Scaling: the 3/8-1.0 cell cannot shrink without a denser, stronger core, and SR-200 stops at 0.508 mm, so core physics survives only at full thickness. My FE: 5 m caps match the sphere within 1.4%; 5052-O alone keeps the face-yield ratio (0.99), elastic gamma within 3-4%. Adverse pre-test prediction: at 042's 9.3-16.1 mm tolerance the 028b section reaches elastic gamma 0.47-0.51, and its core passes CR III shear strength at 25-38 kPa. Gamma 0.564 needs dimples of at most 5.8 mm, the core 2.4 mm, the faces 1.3 mm. The outcome table maps each gamma band to R10/R30. Three articles per configuration discriminate models; statistical bounds need far more, so results count through a validated FE. First: the dimple specification, 038 T1, core witnesses, rig safety. Twelve NFI. Next: none.

source_report_body: MAINLINE-058 filed, QUESTIONABLE/PROJECTION. My own P2 model reproduces 050's five fixed hulls exactly; P3 comes from 052's rows. Two levers widen the band. Relief: size the hull for the -30 hPa day, then climb (or admit air) above it. The worst-corner hot edge rises 11.9-12.0 K for P2 and 6.4-6.6 K for P3, P2's hull is 4.5-4.7% lighter, and there is no upper pressure limit. Thrust buys about 0.6 K for an hour, a kite helps only tethered hulls, shade nothing. At London Heathrow 2014-2023, 24-hour days covered: P2 R10 34% as built, 64% relieved, 84% with the finish, R12 96%; P3 sized at standard pressure and climbing, 78% (R10) and 97% (R12). 95% of days needs R12 with gamma/Q/film (P2) or S/F/J (P3); 99% needs R20 (P2) or R15 (P3). claim: Carry CHECK-059's 99%-removal times, two-coat Ultra-Ever Dry bill and unreproduced P3 ponding; 0.1 kg/m² stays provisional.
source_report_body:
QUESTIONABLE/PROJECTION. MAINLINE-059 complete.

What stays on (a Furmidge drop model calibrated on a measured plate; five finishes): P2's smooth hull keeps 0.014-0.051 kg/m2 after rain with 10 min drainage (upper reading x1.48) and 0.011-0.056 after dew.

P3's film bays sag into dishes under vacuum (024: 9.9 cm crown on 2.32 m bays at R10), so its top bays pond rain. That is 37 kg mean over frame orientations at R10, ranging 5-171 (node on top 55, bay on top 171), and it scales as R cubed.

How fast: an energy balance (checked against 050 and FAO-56) dries P2's residue in 0.2-1.0 h at fair midday and 0.6-7.7 h on a fair morning. Ponds need 65-465 h.

Capacity (own model, cure included): P2 carries 0.1945 kg/m2 in all at R10 ISA and 1.127 at R30. 1 mm floats only at R30 ISA. P3 carries 0.1246 at R10 (052).

Answer: P2 keeps the 0.1 kg/m2 design load and holds it by waiting, at no mass cost. Topcoats add 16-47 kg to save 8-17 kg; heater film adds 503 kg.

P3 carries 0.1 kg/m2 only if its ponds are emptied: with a bay on top, R10 sinks (210 against 157 kg). The cheapest fix is to put a node on top and tip the hull past 14 deg after rain. A night shelter (about 4.9M RUB, floor-scaled) is the fallback.

Ground it by weighing a full-scale P2 panel and a sagged P3 bay after rain and dew. 12 NFI.

The card's arithmetic and lead results reproduce: 64 of 66 normalisations exactly (the two widths follow 015's nu 0.30, as stated); weak-meridian endpoints 78.631/90.736 kPa against 78.627/90.722, all 14 within 0.032%, each a true limit point, unchanged on 4x meshes; eigenpressures within 0.0063% on the owner's meshes; face stresses within 1.7%; transfer40 within 0.15%; 21 arithmetic items. (2) The card's core law (in-plane E 0.01 MPa) loses ellipticity at 0.088 MPa shear, reached at 7-11 kPa; refined meshes go unstable on the flank below the endpoints, but stay stable to the limits at 1 MPa.
